newsitem.title: UK: Camilla heirlooms snapped up at auction.
newsitem.headline: Camilla heirlooms snapped up at auction.

text.p: Family heirlooms belonging to Prince Charles' lover, Camilla Parker Bowles, were snapped up at a London auction on Wednesday, with some items selling for more than treble pre-sale estimates.
The collection of urns, goblets, candlesticks and bowls raised 30,000 pounds ($47,550) for Parker Bowles, who was divorced last year.
"They have well exceeded expectations. A lot of them have trebled in estimate, or more in some cases," said a spokeswoman for Christie's auction house.
"There was frenzied telephone bidding," she added.

At Parker Bowles' request, the auction house took the unusual step of including her name in the catalogue for the goods, made from Blue John, a type of Fluorospar found only in Derbyshire, northern England. It said Parker Bowles had inherited the collection from her maternal grandmother, eldest daughter of Alice Keppel, who in a strange twist was for many years the mistress of a previous Prince of Wales, who later became King Edward VII.
Parker Bowles is said to have reminded Charles, the current Prince of Wales, of this fact when she first met him in 1971.
Her relationship with heir to the throne Charles has been widely blamed for the breakdown of his marriage to Princess Diana, which ended in divorce in August. ($1=.6309 Pound)
